column1: Country names are based largely on ISO 3166-1 specifications.
GEM has made a few additions to the list of countries specifed in ISO 3166-1 (e.g., including Kosovo).
GEM has also made modifications of a few of the country names from what is specified in ISO 3166-1, typically to shorten the name to reflect more common usage.

The ISO data in this tab is drawn from Wikipedia. Subsequently, GEM purchased the official ISO 3166 data set, so these could be compared against the Wikipedia version to ensure that everything attributed to ISO does in fact match the official version.

Other notes:
* GEM recognizes the Russian occupied territory in the country of Ukraine as being part of Ukraine and not Russia, including Crimea and the Donbass Region
* GEM recognizes the autonomy of the following countries: Kosovo, Palestine, Taiwan, Western Sahara
Country subdivisions are largely based on ISO 3166-2 specifications.

We are standardizing our subnational divisions in line with ISO 3166-2 as of April 2026, and this will be implemented in the database soon. We have followed the ISO standard for the subdivisions themselves for every country (with three exceptions, detailed below). However, we have deviated from the names for those subdivisions in particular cases, based on regional expert feedback about the most commonly recognized names. Some countries had more than one level subnational divisions in the ISO standard, and we chose the highest level that is commonly used. (Lower levels can be specified in other fields, such as "major area.")

The exceptions in which we have not used the subdivisions in the ISO standard are:
1. Monaco: This is a city-state which has subnational divisions in the ISO standard that amount to specific neighborhoods, a level of granularity that didn't fit with what is generally regarded as a "subnational division." In the standard, other similarly small countries did not have subnational divisions.
2. Norway: There are more up-to-date subnational divisions that the country has implemented, but that are not reflected in the ISO standard.
3. Western Sahara: This disputed area is recognized as a country in the ISO standard, but its subdivisions aren't included in the ISO 3166-2 standard, so we included some of its provinces in the GEM standard. This could use more work, but there are very few projects that we track in this country.

Correction on 2026-08-06 GOGET researcher spotted an issue with the names for two Russian subnational units. Krasnodar and Krasnoyarsk were flipped. The GEM Subnat code and coordinates align. This has now been corrected in this file, and will be corrected in the microservice that generates responses in the database, and the boundary data.
